A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 26-page versions of the same paper. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian simulations and experiments on Adult and two COMPAS tasks, including market-share, welfare, and convergence results in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and real-data experiments, including the results in Section 6 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The best-response procedure, inverse-competition example weights, and weighted empirical risk minimization in Section 5, Equations 10–11, are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian simulations, Adult, COMPAS-Arrest, and COMPAS-Violent tasks, including the same feature-availability and asymmetric-information scenarios in Appendix D.

E2.justification: The initial accuracy-maximizing classifier remains the reference for reported gains. No comparison method is added or removed from the main or appendix experiments.

E3.justification: Preprocessing, model configurations, metrics, provider counts, and feature settings remain identical. Appendix C retains the same 20% test and 20% validation allocations.

E4.justification: The order-of-play, training-versus-test dynamics, feature-availability, asymmetric-data, and Gaussian-overlap analyses in Section 6 and Appendix D are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten random data splits and the same standard-error reporting practice, including Table 5. No run-count or uncertainty-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 2–6 and plotted results in Figures 1–8 match. Findings about convergence, market share, order of play, and welfare are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, theoretical statements, and derivations in Sections 3–5 are unchanged, as are the proofs in Appendix A and congestion-game characterization in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about competition-aware learning, welfare, rapid convergence, and the importance of move timing.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations concerning shared data distributions, transparency, rational user choice, and real-market applicability remain identical. Renaming the impact section does not change its content.

D1.justification: Section 6 replaces the code repository pointer Ohadeinav/competition_games with BML-Technion/market4acc and adds 'publicly' to its availability statement. Appendix C's implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs establish no change to repository contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to competitive learning, strategic classification, and performative prediction are unchanged. The new publication footer does not revise research positioning.

P1.justification: The preprint notice becomes an ICML 2025 proceedings notice, 'Broader impact' becomes 'Impact Statement,' and the code-availability sentence is lightly edited. The substantive prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The publication footer causes limited text reflow across pages 1–3, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. All figures, tables, and appendix layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: The scientific arguments, empirical evidence, limitations, and appendices are unchanged. The revised repository pointer and publication-format edits provide no demonstrated material quality gain or loss; both versions already supplied code-access information.
